docs.title: Derived Parameters
docs.text: Derived parameters are user-defined per-event formulas (e.g. [FITC-A] / [APC-A]) exposed as extra channels. This page covers how they're modelled, the one rule every data-loading path must follow, and where the pieces live. For the user-facing behaviour see Derived Parameters.

docs.title: Design in one paragraph
docs.text: A derived parameter is appended to each sample as an extra column in fcs_data.events and an extra key in fcs_data.channels. Almost everything downstream — axis dropdowns, gates (Gate.contains looks columns up by name), propagation, dag_evaluator, statistics, comparisons — already works by channel name, so it works with derived parameters unchanged. The column is never persisted and never written to raw_events; it's recomputed from the current event table whenever that table changes.

docs.title: Module map
docs.text: Module Responsibility analysis/derived/expression.py Formula language: parse_formula() → DerivedExpression (channels, evaluate(df)), FormulaError(message, position). analysis/derived/models.py DerivedParameter (stored definition), DerivedParameterDraft (editor input), is_derived_key(), new_param_id(). analysis/derived/sync.py sync_fcs_data(), sync_sample(), sync_experiment(), strip_derived_columns(). analysis/derived/state.py DerivedColumnsState — per-FCSData bookkeeping owned by sync. analysis/derived/templates.py, preview.py Editor helpers (Qt-free). Not exported from the package __init__, so the light import chain through fcs_io doesn't pull in scipy. analysis/services/derived_parameter_service.py Validation, create/update/delete, find_dependents(), publishes DERIVED_PARAMS_CHANGED. analysis/channel_inference.py DerivedAwareChannelInference — derived axes default to their preferred linear/log scale. ui/widgets/derived_formula_editor.py, ui/dialogs/derived_parameter_dialog.py, ui/widgets/mini_histogram.py Editor, non-modal manager dialog, preview histogram. ui/controllers/derived_editor_controller.py Owns the dialog; puts a parameter created from a graph's axis dropdown onto that axis.

docs.title: Keys, persistence and gates
docs.text:
• Column key: derived:<8 hex> (constants.DERIVED_PREFIX). Gates, axis memory and channel scales reference the key, so renaming a parameter never breaks them. Display labels (ƒ <name>) come from get_channel_marker_label() / derived_labels_of().
  • Definitions live on Experiment.derived_parameters and are serialized by ExperimentSerializer under "derived_parameters" (absent → []).
  • Gate record: Gate.derived_formulas snapshots the formula of any derived axis when the gate is created (GateCoordinator.add_gate). It's display/audit only — evaluation always uses the current definition — and is serialized only when non-empty, so ordinary gates serialize exactly as before. gate_from_dict() restores it centrally.
  • Derived parameters can't reference other derived parameters (rejected by DerivedParameterService.canonicalize).

docs.title: The sync contract
docs.text:
Rule

Any code that replaces sample.fcs_data, or assigns sample.fcs_data.events, must call sync_sample(experiment, sample) (or sync_experiment(experiment)) before anything evaluates gates.

Current call sites:

Path Where New sample added Experiment.add_sample() Compensation apply / toggle CompensationView._on_apply_all, _on_toggle_compensation Workspace reload WorkflowService.reload_fcs_data — before on_complete evaluates gates State restore (undo/redo, workflow load) FlowStore.restore, WorkflowService.reload_fcs_data Definition created / edited / deleted DerivedParameterService._after_change Safety nets PopulationService.get_gated_events, GateCoordinator.recompute_all_stats

How sync stays correct and cheap:

  • Idempotent, zero-cost when unused. sync_sample() returns immediately when the experiment has no definitions and the frame has no derived columns — workspaces that never use the feature never touch this code.
  • Swap, don't mutate. Sync builds a new DataFrame and assigns it to fcs_data.events. Concurrent readers never see a half-written column, and GateNode mask caches (keyed on frame identity) miss naturally.
  • Replaced frames are detected, not trusted. DerivedColumnsState.frame_ref is a weak reference to the frame sync last produced. Any other frame is treated as fresh base data and fully recomputed — even if it carries copies of old derived columns (e.g. apply_compensation copying events when there's no raw backup; it also strips them itself).
  • Signatures (formula | positive_denominators) detect definition edits on an unchanged frame, so only edited columns are recomputed.
  • Missing inputs → NaN column, never a missing column, so gates on the parameter can't raise KeyError on a sample that lacks a channel.

docs.title: Numeric semantics
docs.text:
• Evaluation is vectorized float64 under np.errstate(all="ignore"); ±inf becomes NaN.
  • positive_denominators=True turns any division by a value ≤ 0 into NaN.
  • NaN fails every gate comparison and is dropped by compute_statistic (dropna), auto-range (isfinite) and pseudocolor rendering.
  • apply_transform() preserves NaN (Logicle would otherwise map it to ≈ −1 display units, which would plot — and gate — invalid events at the axis floor).
  • Only linear and log scales are offered: Logicle's parameter estimation assumes a ~262k fluorescence range.
  • Log floor. log_transform clamps values below min_value (1.0 for detectors), which would put every ratio < 1 on one point. AxisScale.log_floor carries the floor; AxisManager gives derived keys DERIVED_LOG_FLOOR (1e-6), and every transform call site gets it via get_transform_kwargs() / log_transform_kwargs() (CoordinateMapper, project_to_display for gates, RenderTask). Log-axis ticks are the decades within the visible range (log_decade_tick_values), not the fixed 10³–10⁵. The Comparisons histogram overlay has no AxisScale; it lowers the floor only when the pooled data's median is below 1.

docs.title: Formula language
docs.text: [channel] references (channel name or unambiguous marker label — the service canonicalizes to channel names), numbers, + - * / ^ **, unary minus, parentheses, and the whitelisted functions in expression._FUNCTIONS. It's parsed with ast and compiled to closures; user text never reaches eval/pd.eval. Limits: 500 characters, 50 channel references, nesting depth 32. To add a function, add it to _FUNCTIONS (name → numpy callable, arity) and a case to tests/unit/analysis/derived/test_expression.py.

docs.title: Events and UI
docs.text:
events.DERIVED_PARAMS_CHANGED ({"param_id", "action"} with action ∈ created/updated/deleted) is published after every sample has been re-synced:

  • HistoryRecorder records an undo step (created/updated/deleted — not synced), and MainPanelController calls _on_derived_params_changed (refreshes Statistics/Comparisons pickers, hierarchy, node canvas; recomputes stats for samples with gates on an edited parameter).
  • Each GraphWindow rebuilds its own axis lists — falling back to FSC-A/SSC-A if its axis was deleted, re-rendering if its axis was edited.
  • The dialog refreshes its list (e.g. after undo).

The "＋ New derived parameter…" entry is a sentinel item (NEW_DERIVED_SENTINEL) appended by AxisControlPanel.add_new_derived_entry(); picking it snaps the combo back and emits new_derived_requested(axis) → GraphWindow.derived_editor_requested → GraphManager.derived_editor_requested → DerivedEditorController.open_for_axis.

Channel consumers intentionally differ: get_fluorescence_channels() excludes derived keys (so UMAP, compensation and the multi-channel Comparisons plots never see them); direct fcs_data.channels listings (axes, Statistics, single-channel Comparisons) include them.

docs.title: Academy
docs.text: Course 6's derived-parameter block (c6_d01–c6_d13, plus c6_s06a_ratio_channel) uses DerivedRatioExistsValidator, DerivedEditorClosedValidator, ActiveGraphDerivedAxisValidator and StatsDerivedChannelValidator. They match on the saved canonical formula, not the name the learner chose. Steps inside the dialog use plain target_widget_names: the dialog is its own window, and since SDK 2.4.0 the Academy driver frames targets in other windows inside that window. tests/unit/tutorials/test_course_step_graph.py checks every course for dangling or unreachable steps.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
• tests/unit/analysis/derived/ — expression, sync, service, integration hooks (compensation, reload, gates, templates), templates/preview, inference strategy; shared make_fcs/make_sample fixtures in its conftest.py.
  • tests/ui/test_derived_parameter_ui.py — editor, dialog flows, axis-dropdown entry, controller, ribbon button, GraphWindow.

docs.title: 10. State, Undo/Redo & Persistence
docs.text: How the flow module keeps one source of truth, turns edits into undo steps, knows when the workspace is unsaved, and saves/loads it — and the rules new code has to follow so all of that keeps working.

docs.title: 1. The single source of truth
docs.text:
FlowState (analysis/state.py) holds the whole session: state.data (experiment, compensation, UMAP runs) and state.view (selection and display settings). One instance lives for the whole session. Loads and undo/redo change its contents in place; state, state.data and state.view are never replaced, so the ~40 services and widgets that receive state in their constructor can keep that reference forever.

What does get replaced is state.data.experiment — and with it every Sample, Group and GateNode object. So:

Never cache a Sample, Group or GateNode across a user action. Keep ids (sample_id, node_id) and look objects up through state when you need them.

GraphWindow is the model to follow: it stores sample_id/node_id and resolves the sample on every render.

docs.title: 2. The one serializer
docs.text:
analysis/workspace_document.py is the only code that turns the workspace into plain data or back:

Function Used by Shape serialize_workspace / apply_workspace WorkflowService save/load, FlowState.to_dict/from_dict the workflow document: experiment, compensation, view (WorkflowService adds sample_paths and binary attachments around it) capture_model / model_experiment FlowStore (undo history) the model snapshot: experiment (minus scales/axis memory), compensation, UMAP run ids

apply_workspace replaces the entire previous workspace — including UMAP runs, the group filter, the FMO overlay and fallback scales — and view defaults come from a fresh ViewState(), so a load and a new workspace always agree. The persisted view fields are listed once, in PERSISTED_VIEW_FIELDS.

Adding a persisted field means adding it to ExperimentSerializer (model) or PERSISTED_VIEW_FIELDS (view) — nowhere else. test_workspace_document.py fails if a field doesn't round-trip exactly.

docs.title: 3. What undo covers
docs.text:
Kind of change Examples Undoable Marks unsaved Analysis model gates, logic wiring, samples, groups, roles, markers, compensation, derived parameters, UMAP runs ✅ ✅ Display settings & annotations channel scales/transforms, render settings, UMAP cluster names/custom clusters ❌ ✅ Navigation selected sample/gate, active tab, per-sample last-viewed axes, default axis params ❌ ❌

Channel scales aren't undoable because rendering writes auto-ranged defaults into them (AxisManager.get_scale materializes a default on first read), so every first draw would otherwise look like a user edit.

docs.title: 4. FlowStore — history over the live state
docs.text:
analysis/store.py. Owns an SDK UndoHistory of model snapshots; the panel binds it with PluginBase.bind_undo_history(store.history, store.restore), which is what Edit → Undo/Redo (Cmd/Ctrl+Z, Cmd+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y) and the menu labels ("Undo Delete Gate") run on.

  • commit(label) — record the current state as one step.
  • absorb() — fold the current state into the latest step. For background follow-ups to a user action (gate propagation to other samples lands ~300 ms after the edit): undoing the edit undoes both.
  • mark_unsaved_change() — a saved-but-not-undoable change (display settings, UMAP cluster names).
  • batch(label) / pause()/resume() — coalesce, or stop recording across a multi-turn operation (a workflow load).
  • restore(snapshot) — rebuild the experiment from a snapshot, reattach what snapshots only reference by id (event data, UMAP embeddings, group scales — cached by the store and released once no reachable step needs them), recompute compensated event data where it no longer matches the restored compensation flags/matrix (Apply/Toggle Compensation rewrite fcs_data.events in place), repair view pointers that no longer resolve, and publish STATE_RESTORED.
  • record_unannounced_changes() — safety net run before every undo/redo/save: a live change that no event announced becomes its own "Edit" step (and logs a warning) instead of being merged into — and lost with — the previous one.

docs.title: Unsaved changes
docs.text:
store.is_dirty = a saved-but-not-undoable change was made or the current history step isn't the saved one. Because it's revision-based, undoing back to the saved step reads as clean again. A save calls panel._begin_save() when it starts and panel._finish_save(token) when it succeeds: edits made while a background save runs stay dirty.

Everything that cares about unsaved changes reads store.is_dirty:

  • the Save Workspace button (via the store's dirty listener);
  • closing the window — the SDK's isolated window calls panel.confirm_close(), which offers Save / Discard / Cancel. Save runs the normal background save and closes once _finish_save sees it succeed; a cancelled or failed save just means the next close asks again. A close the Hub requests is never prompted;
  • loading a workflow over unsaved edits (e.g. the Hub injecting another one) asks "Discard and load" / Cancel first;
  • the SDK's 15-minute autosave (has_unsaved_changes=) skips a tick entirely — no rewrite, no reminder toast — when nothing changed.

docs.title: 5. Recording edits — HistoryRecorder
docs.text:
analysis/history_recorder.py is the one table mapping domain events to the store (STEP_EVENTS, ABSORB_EVENTS, UNTRACKED_EVENTS). MainPanelController.wire() starts it.

CentralEventBus delivers synchronously on the GUI thread, and one user action often publishes several events (a quadrant creates four nodes; a rename is applied across samples). The recorder therefore defers the commit to the end of the event-loop turn: everything requested in one turn is one step, named by the first request. Undo, redo and save flush() it first.

Adding a new kind of edit: non-gate edits live in analysis/services/experiment_edits.py (samples, groups, roles, templates, compensation, UMAP runs) — each function mutates state by id and then announces itself with MODEL_EDITED plus the UI-refresh events widgets already listen for. Widgets call these; they never mutate the experiment directly. A new edit either goes there or, at minimum, ends with

experiment_edits.announce("Rename Group")          # one undo step
experiment_edits.announce_unsaved_change()         # saved, not undoable

Gate edits go through GateCoordinator as before (their events are already in STEP_EVENTS). Address samples/groups/nodes by id in any callback — a captured object is detached by the next undo.

docs.title: 6. Reacting to undo/redo — STATE_RESTORED
docs.text:
After a restore every model object is new. The panel's _on_state_restored cancels pending propagation, recomputes statistics, calls GraphManager.reconcile_with_state() (closes graphs whose sample/population is gone, reloads the rest by id) and refreshes every widget. A widget that keeps model-derived state of its own must refresh it from state here.

Undo/redo also first cancel any half-finished gate drag, and are refused while a workflow is loading or a save is running.

docs.title: 7. Workflow load lifecycle
docs.text:
1. load_workflow → _begin_workflow_load(): flush any pending step, store.pause(), cancel propagation.
  2. WorkflowService.load_workflow → apply_workspace (whole workspace replaced in place) → background FCS reload → attachments.
  3. _on_fcs_done → _finish_workflow_load(clean=True): resume and store.reset() — the loaded workflow is the clean baseline, with nothing to undo into the previous workspace.

A failed load resets to an unsaved baseline; a reload task that errors is reported as every sample failing (so the load still completes); and only the load actually in progress can reset history — a stray late callback can't wipe edits made since.

Tests: tests/unit/analysis/test_store.py, test_history_recorder.py, test_workspace_document.py, tests/ui/test_workflow_load_unload.py, tests/ui/test_undo_restore_ui.py.

docs.title: Plan: active, question-based learning in the Flow Academy
docs.text:
Status: Phases 1–2 merged (SDK 2.4.0, flow #4); Phases 3–7 done on feature/academy-course-plumbing and released as flow 0.11.0 (2026-10-01); Phase 8's numbers test is still open. Resume from the first unchecked checkpoint in Phases and checkpoints.

Released so far: SDK 2.3.0 (QuestionStep, SDK #14); flow 0.10.0 (flow #2), plus the first Course 4 questions merged to main (flow #3).

Branches: one per phase in each repo, each merged before the next starts. Phase 2: SDK and flow feature/academy-popup-highlights (SDK 2.4.0).

Why: the professors asked for more active learning. Today the courses explain and the learner clicks; they rarely have to think. We want:

  • Questions the learner must answer correctly to move on. Single-choice or select-all-that-apply, about what's on screen or what was just covered.
  • Question now, answer later. Ask a prediction ("which hump will the T cells be in?"), let the learner find out, and pay it off, sometimes a whole course later. Course 1's spleen/thymus/bone-marrow mystery, solved in Course 2, is the model.
  • No longer courses. Steps get more concise, with the learning built into them. Course 4 (80 steps) should get shorter.

It also covers two points from the course review: Course 4's feature-tour feel, and highlights drawn on the wrong window for targets inside popups.

docs.title: 1. Principles
docs.text:
1. Every question earns its place. It tests something the learner needs later or checks a misconception that is common in real analysis. No trivia about where a button is.
  2. Replace explanations with questions, don't add to them. A step that explains "dead cells take up PI, so they're bright" becomes "Which peak are the dead cells?" The explanation moves into the answer feedback.
  3. Wrong answers teach. Every wrong option has its own feedback explaining why it's wrong. The learner retries until correct. After 2 wrong attempts, the correct option is highlighted, but they still have to pick it, so there's no dead end.
  4. Short. Question ≤ 50 words, each option ≤ 15 words, feedback ≤ 40 words (enforced by a test).
  5. On-screen questions spotlight what to look at, and leave the UI usable (allow_interaction=True) so the learner can hover, zoom or switch a dropdown before answering.
  6. Numbers in questions come from the tutorial data, checked by a test (see §6). Never "about 60%" from memory.

docs.title: 2. SDK: a QuestionStep (Karcytics-SDK)
docs.text:
BranchingStep is not enough. It renders options as footer buttons, title-cases their labels, and has no notion of a correct answer. So we add a new step type in karcytics_sdk/plugin/tutorial_models.py:

@dataclass
class AnswerOption:
    text: str
    correct: bool = False
    feedback: str = ""          # shown when this option is chosen (why right / why wrong)

@dataclass
class QuestionStep(BaseStep):   # text = the question
    options: list[AnswerOption] = field(default_factory=list)
    multi_select: bool = False  # "select all that apply"
    kind: str = "check"         # "check" (must be correct) | "predict" (any answer, revealed later)
    question_id: str = ""       # stable key for recording the answer (predictions, analytics)
    explanation: str = ""       # shown once answered correctly, before Continue
    reveal_after_attempts: int = 2

Behaviour: - Options render as radio buttons (or checkboxes) in the bubble body, with a Check button in the footer. Next stays hidden until the answer is correct. - Wrong: show that option's feedback, then retry. Multi-select wrong answers say "one or more are wrong" plus the feedback for the first wrong pick, so the learner isn't told the whole answer. - After reveal_after_attempts wrong tries: the correct option(s) are outlined, and the learner must still select them. - Correct: show explanation, then Continue → next_step_id. - kind="predict": any answer is accepted, and the Continue label says "Let's find out". The answer is recorded for a later reveal. - Keyboard: 1–9 toggles an option, Enter checks.

Recorded answers: AcademyManager.answers[course_id][question_id] = {choice, attempts, correct}, persisted in progress.json. This powers two things: - Reveals: a later step's text can reference the learner's answer, e.g. {answer:c1_q_mystery} in text. Because answers are persisted, this works across courses. - Future reporting: optional per-question attempt counts for the professors. Not built now, but stored so it's possible later.

Validation (in __post_init__): - At least 2 options. - Single-select: exactly one correct. - Multi-select: at least one correct. - check questions: every wrong option has feedback. - predict questions: no correct flags needed.

Tests: model validation, overlay rendering (radio vs. checkbox, Check/Continue, wrong-answer feedback, reveal after N attempts), manager recording and persistence, and {answer:…} substitution.

Release: needs an SDK minor bump (2.1.9 → 2.2.0) and the plugin's karcytics-sdk>=2.2.0 pin.

docs.title: 3. SDK: highlight targets inside popups (review point 4)
docs.text:
The Academy overlay lives in the main window, so a target inside a separate window is spotlit on the main window underneath it. We fixed this for the Derived Parameters dialog with a plugin-side hook (ui/widgets/tutorial_highlight.py, metadata["in_window_targets"]).

Other popups are parented the same way and likely have the same bug:

Popup Steps affected Population picker c4_s05, c4_s17b, c4_s20a Transform dialog c1_s27d, c1_s30d Compensation matrix dialog c1_s15 Quick-Stats grid c2_s50b–c2_s53b

Plan: 1. Audit those steps in the app. 2. Move TutorialHighlight into the SDK, and make AcademyStepDriver._update_targets split targets by window: the main window gets overlay rects, other windows get in-window frames plus their frame rect so Cyto stays clear. 3. Then drop the plugin's in_window_targets special case; ordinary target_widget_names just works.

docs.title: 4. Making room: conciseness levers
docs.text:
These free about 30 steps across the four courses, so questions fit without growing any course.

Step budget:

Course Now Target Questions (≈) 1 75 ≤ 75 6 2 75 ≤ 72 6 3 69 ≤ 68 6 4 80 ≤ 65 7

docs.title: Course 4: restructured around one question
docs.text:
Driving question, asked at c4_s00_intro as (P): "Are UMAP's B cells and your hand-gated B cells the same cells, measured the same way?" Every section answers part of it, and graduation shows the learner their prediction next to the evidence.

Section Change Derived parameter c4_d08b becomes (P) "Before you switch: which hump will T cells be in?". c4_d13_pitfalls becomes a question: "One population shows 40% invalid — what's wrong?" → dim denominator. The histogram overlay uses ƒ B220/CD45 instead of B220, with a question: "Do both B-cell definitions peak at the same ratio?". Generate/wait pairs are merged. Export 7 steps become 1 checklist step. docs.title: 6. Quality gates
docs.text:
• tests/unit/tutorials/test_course_step_graph.py follows the new link fields (QuestionStep next ids) and checks that every (P) question has a later reveal step referencing its question_id.
  • A new test_question_steps.py covers: SDK validation passes, length limits (§1.4), the question_id is unique across all courses, and there's at least one on-screen question per course.
  • A new test_tutorial_numbers.py recomputes the numbers quoted in questions and steps from the tutorial FCS files (e.g. B220/CD45 medians, % Total by sample, AND-node overlap) and fails if the text drifts from the data. It needs a small NUMBERS table that course text formats from.
  • Per phase, the user plays the changed course end to end (the only way to catch overlay/visual issues; see the step 15 spotlight bug).

docs.title: Phases and checkpoints
docs.text:
Each phase is one commit on a single branch per repo (see the memory note on phase commits), then a play-through checkpoint by the user before the next phase starts.

  • [x] Phase 0: land the current work. SDK 2.2.0 (including the spotlight repaint fix) merged as SDK PR #13. Flow work on feature/undo-redo-integration, bumped to 0.10.0, is in flow PR #2.
  • [x] Phase 1: SDK QuestionStep (§2) plus tests. Merged: SDK #14 (2.3.0), flow #3. In place of a sandbox course, two real Course 4 questions were added for trying it in the app: c4_d14_invalid_question and c4_s04b_median_question. Checkpoint: user plays Course 4 up to the Statistics tab and settles the look. Done 2026-10-01 as an automated offscreen walk-through (below).
  • [x] Phase 2: SDK cross-window highlights (§3), then remove the plugin's in_window_targets special case. feature/academy-popup-highlights (SDK 2.4.0). Checkpoint: popup steps in Courses 1, 2 and 4 highlight correctly. Done 2026-10-01: the real panel, loaded from a saved Courses 1–3 workspace, was driven offscreen through every Course 4 step (all but the final Save, which needs the Hub) plus the Course 1 Transforms and Course 2 Quick-Stats popups, with a screenshot per step. It found and fixed: a scrolled-out target framed over the dialog's buttons, and sidebar targets spotlit off-screen (targets are now scrolled into view once per step); question feedback clipped after a wrong-then-right answer; Course 1's unnamed Outliers dropdown (now guarded by test_target_names.py); and Course 2/4 text claiming gates propagate only to Samples A–C (they reach every sample in the group, so the B-cells row checks all 10).
  • [x] Phase 3: course plumbing. Tab-switch and generate/wait collapses (§4) across all four courses; step-graph test updates. Checkpoint: quick run of each course's first half. Done: all 13 tab switches are one interactive VerificationStep on the tab bar (no "Checking tab…" or "Oops!" steps), and Course 4's Compute and five Generate steps wait on their own validator (no "Rendering…" step). Steps (total / main path): Course 1 75→73 / 60, Course 2 75→70 / 61, Course 3 69→65 / 63→61, Course 4 84→70 / 78→68. Tabs saved fewer main-path steps than the ~25 estimated: in Courses 1–2 the click step was already off the main path. Checked with a full Course 4 walk-through and a Course 2 tab step on the real panel.
  • [x] Phase 4: Course 4 restructure plus questions (§5). Checkpoint: full play-through. Done: 56 main-path steps (from 68), 7 questions. Changes from the §5 draft, after checking the data:
    • The opening prediction (c4_same_measure) asks whether the two B-cell methods measure the same on B220, since Course 3 already shows they're the same cells. It's revealed at the histogram overlay and at graduation.
    • c4_d08q is a check question, not a prediction: learners can reason it out from what B220 marks.
    • c4_d13_pitfalls stays an InfoStep; making it a question put three questions in four steps.
    • The % Parent question (c4_s06q) replaces the old stats theory step, and the table now uses % Parent and CV instead of % Total and CV. That also drops the subsample star: UMAP B Cells' % Parent is a share of the Leukocytes UMAP ran on, so it compares directly with B-cells' % of Leukocytes (64% vs 68%).
    • The chart-type question ("which charts keep long names readable?") felt awkward in play-through, so it was replaced with an on-screen CV question: Sample B's B-cells have the lowest CV on the ratio, so what does that mean? It's followed by one Heatmap step.
    • Exports are one ForcedInteractionStep with two checked subtasks (Comparisons plot, Statistics CSV); the tabs record successful exports in completed_exports.
    • Verified with a full offscreen walk-through to completion, including graduation.
  • [x] Phase 5: Course 1 questions. Checkpoint: play-through. Done: six questions, as drafted. The thymus prediction (c1_thymus_few) is revealed in Course 2's c2_s54_mystery_reveal alongside Sample A's 0.3% B-cells; Phase 6 may move it when c2_s51–c2_s53 become questions. The spillover, debris, PI and % Total questions replace their InfoSteps and keep the content that mattered in the explanation (single stains drive the matrix; the Cells gate and Biexponential notes; Event Count and Group Preview). The FMO question sits after the roles intro. Steps: 73→75 total (the budget), 60→62 main path. Choices, feedback and explanations render as plain text, so test_answer_text_is_plain rejects markdown there. Checked offscreen: every question answered wrong then right on the real panel (debris on the Blank's FSC/SSC plot, PI on the PI sample at Cells), plus the Course 2 reveal showing the recorded answer.
  • [x] Phase 6: Course 2 questions, including the Course 1 → 2 prediction reveal. Checkpoint: play-through. Done: seven questions, all replacing InfoSteps, so Course 2 stays at 70 steps (61 main path). T-cell location (c2_s06), why the FMO sets the B220 threshold (c2_s17, select all), histogram vs scatter (c2_s19), the CD4+ quadrant (c2_s38, with the Q1–Q4 map in the explanation), and one organ question per sample in the open Quick-Stats grid (c2_s51–c2_s53). The questions make learners read the grid rather than stating the numbers. The play-through also caught the grid's old description: samples are its columns and every cell is % Parent, not rows and % Total, so all four Quick-Stats steps and the reveal (Sample A's B-cells: 0.4% of Leukocytes) now say so. The Course 1 prediction stays revealed in c2_s54. Before this phase, two changes after the Course 1 play-through:
    • Gate checks loosened (user request): polygon overlap 80% (was 90%); range and rectangle edges within 10% of the axis or 35% of the edge's own value, whichever is larger, so high edges on log axes have room; quadrant crosshairs get a quarter of the target window's width as margin on each side. Low edges keep the axis-wide band only, so a B-cells threshold can't creep into the B cells.
    • Correct answers no longer always come first. The SDK shows choices in source order, and every check question in Courses 1 and 4 had the answer first. Positions now vary, and test_correct_answer_position_varies keeps it that way. Checked offscreen on the real panel: every Course 2 question answered wrong then right, with the plot or Quick-Stats grid it refers to on screen.

Done: five check questions replace their InfoSteps (UMAP axes c3_s05, why gate to Leukocytes c3_s10 (select all), why exclude CD45 c3_s12, Neighbors for a rare population c3_s14, what HDBSCAN clusters c3_s21), and the overlap prediction (c3_umap_in_gate) sits after the AND-node plan (c3_s51b2), revealed at the top of c3_s56. Changes from the draft:
    • HDBSCAN's answer is "the same marker data UMAP read", not "the original 6-D data": it clusters UMAP's input matrix (hdbscan_space="high_dim"), which is four markers once PI and CD45 are excluded. c3_s27b's "6-channel similarity" became "marker similarity" for the same reason.
    • The two results sub-tab switches (Interactive Map, Population Statistics) still had Phase 3's old click / "Checking tab…" / "Oops!" triple; each is now one interactive VerificationStep on ClusterResultsTabBar. That pays for the prediction step.
    • Real numbers on Sample C: 99.95% of UMAP B Cells fall inside the hand-gated B-cells, and the scaled estimate covers about 93% of B-cells. Steps: 65→62 total, 61→60 main path. Checked offscreen on the real panel: every question answered wrong then right, a real UMAP + HDBSCAN run with both sub-tab steps advancing on the click (and passing straight through when the tab is already open), and the reveal showing the recorded prediction over the AND node.
  • [ ] Phase 8: numbers test (§6), user docs (docs/user/10_ACADEMY_TUTORIALS.md), and the flow plugin version bump that releases it (the SDK side shipped as 2.4.0 in Phase 1–2). The user docs and the bump (0.11.0, min_core_version 2.0.7) shipped with Phase 7; only the numbers test remains.

docs.title: Decisions (2026-10-01)
docs.text:
1. Wrong answers: the learner must select the correct answer to continue. It's outlined after 2 wrong tries, but they still have to pick it.
  2. Recording: attempts per question are saved locally only (progress.json); no export.
  3. Radar chart: drop its steps from Course 4, but explain what it's for in one sentence: comparing populations' whole marker profiles at once (shape = profile). Point learners to it for many-marker panels.

docs.title: Plan: teach the new Compensation tab (Courses 1–2 become 1–3)
docs.text:
Status: plan only, nothing built. Resume from the first unchecked box in Phases and checkpoints.

Why: the Compensation tab now has selectable methods, a Method setup page, the FMO method with its step-by-step illustration, before/after previews across samples, fine-tuning, and a matrix library. Course 1 still teaches the old tab in 8 steps, and its Apply step points at a button on a page that isn't open. The gating order also changes: Cells gate → compensation → Live Cells, because the FMO fit runs on the Cells gate and Live Cells is gated on a compensated channel.

Constraints (from the user): - Every course stays at 55–70 steps (total, side branches included). - Order in the first course: setup, Cells gate, singlets explained, then compensation, before any Live Cells gate. - Five courses in total: today's 1 and 2 become 1, 2 and 3; today's 3 and 4 become 4 and 5 unchanged. - The rules of ACADEMY_ACTIVE_LEARNING_PLAN.md still apply: questions replace explanations, quoted numbers come from the data, wrong answers carry feedback.

docs.title: 1. The split
docs.text:
Compensation is cut in two by skill: judging a matrix you already have (Course 1) and building and refining your own (Course 2).

# Course Content Steps (approx.) 1 Setup, first gate & compensation basics Intro 3 · import and roles 14 · Cells gate and singlets 17 · Spectral viewer and masterclass 7 · compensation part A 18 · save and graduation 2 61 2 Building a matrix & clean-up gates Checkpoint and intro 3 · compensation part B 22 · Live Cells 15 · Leukocytes 20 · propagation, save, graduation 3 63 3 Immunophenotyping Today's Course 2 minus its Spectral section (8 steps), plus a reworded recap 62 4 Population analysis Today's Course 3 62 5 Derived parameters & statistics Today's Course 4 56 main path

Step counts for existing sections were counted from the source; new sections are budgets. Each phase re-counts.

Why the Spectral viewer moves to Course 1: it explains why spillover exists, which belongs before the learner reads a matrix, not a whole course after. Its masterclass slideshow ends on "which control tubes would you need to build a matrix?", which sets up Course 2.

docs.title: 2. What the tutorial data offers
docs.text:
Measured on tests/data/fcs/ (FMO fit on all events; re-measure on the Cells gate in Phase 0).

Pair (dye → detector) File's matrix FMO method Use in the course PE → PerCP-Cy5.5 0.300 not estimated (0, greyed) The key hook. There is no PerCP-Cy5.5 FMO, so the FMO method leaves that column empty. PerCP-Cy5.5 is the PI channel, so this cell decides whether PE-bright cells look dead. Pacific Blue → APC-Cy7 0.000 0.051 (earlier runs: about 0.02 on Cells) Shows that "Fit on: Cells" changes the answer. APC → APC-Cy7 0.170 0.194 Two methods, close agreement: what "roughly agree" looks like. PE → FITC 0.030 0.047 Same.

Other facts the course text must respect: - The file's matrix is applied automatically on import (samples show ✦). "Apply to all samples" in Course 1 therefore reports that samples were skipped. - All five FMO tubes are placed from their data; the e450 tube's name does not identify its dye, so it is the natural example for "How we know". - Detection asks that one channel stand clear of the tube's others. The PE tube is the least clear-cut (0.48 as bright as the other FMOs, its next-lowest channel at 1.01) and still places with room to spare.

(on screen; answer 0.30, row = dye, column = detector) Question 15 The status line names the method the numbers came from Info 16 Set the preview to X = PE, Y = PerCP-Cy5.5 Interaction 17 "After compensation, how should a PE-only population sit?" (level, not tilted up) Question 18 View → Scatter + histograms; what the histograms add Interaction + Info 19 Sample → All samples Interaction 20 "Why check every sample, not one?" docs.title: Plan: pause and resume Academy courses (Academy workflows)
docs.text:
Status: built 2026-10-17 and run through offscreen. Commits: SDK 281a1aa, 220428d, 53d64f9, 6df5846; flow 10edcd5, 7b5302c, da1c27d; Hub b694cab on feature/academy-pause-resume. Open: the user's own play-through.

Why: the five flow courses run 58–65 steps each. A learner can't stop partway: closing the module loses their place, and the catalog only knows "not started" or "completed".

Repos and branches: - Karcytics-SDK — commits on main. - Karcytics-flow-cytometry — commits on main. - Karcytics (Hub) — branch feature/academy-pause-resume off the latest develop. - One commit per phase. The user handles version bumps and releases.

docs.title: 1. The model: an Academy workflow
docs.text:
A course always runs inside a saved workflow. Starting a course from the catalog turns the current workflow into an Academy workflow. Cyto says so first, and an unnamed workspace is named and saved at that point. The same workflow carries the learner through all five courses, because each course builds on the one before.

An Academy workflow is in one of four states:

State When What the learner sees running A course is on screen The normal course overlay, plus a ⏸ Pause button paused The learner pressed Pause, closed the window mid-course, or the app quit The panel is dimmed and inert. A centred card shows Cyto waiting, "Ready to continue Course 2: Compensation?", "Step 23 of 60", ▶ Resume and Leave course… between_courses Course N (N < 5) just finished The same locked card: "Course 2 complete — start Course 3?", with ▶ Start Course 3 (default) and Leave Academy graduated Course 5 finished The workflow unlocks. It stays marked as an Academy workflow, with "All courses completed"

Leave course / Leave Academy removes the academy block, so the workflow becomes an ordinary workflow and keeps all its work. This is how a learner stops after N courses to explore on their own. By default, each finished course prompts them into the next one.

A workflow that has an academy block is never interactive outside running, except once graduated.

docs.title: 2. What gets saved, and where
docs.text:
Workflow metadata (metadata["academy"] in the workflow JSON) is the source of truth for resuming:

{
  "academy": {
    "state": "paused",
    "course_id": "flow_course_2_compensation",
    "course_title": "Building a matrix & clean-up gates",
    "course_number": 2,
    "course_count": 5,
    "step_id": "c2_b20_save",
    "step_history": ["c2_s01", "..."],
    "subtask_progress": {},
    "step_number": 23,
    "step_total": 60,
    "completed_courses": ["flow_course_1_fundamentals"],
    "ui": {"tab": 2},
    "updated_at": "2026-10-17T10:00:00+00:00"
  }
}
  • The Hub reads this block directly to draw the dashboard card. It can't ask the plugin, because the plugin process isn't running.
  • _current_workflow_metadata already rides along on Save, Update and autosave, so autosave during a course keeps the block current. If the app crashes, a workflow found in the running state is treated as paused.
  • The step number comes from Course.get_main_path(), the same count the overlay's progress bar uses.

progress.json (the plugin's own Academy data) gains in_progress[course_id] for the catalog: workflow filename, project dir, step number and total, and updated time. The latest attempt wins. Several attempts at the same course may exist in different workflows, and the catalog shows the latest one.

docs.title: 3. Pausing and resuming
docs.text:
Pause: - The ⏸ Pause button in the bubble header replaces the "×" exit, which currently means "lose your place". - Closing the module window mid-course asks first (user's call, 2026-10-17: never save without asking). Save pauses, saves and then closes; Don't Save closes with nothing saved, so the course later resumes from the last save; Cancel keeps the window open. - The catalog's progress for an attempt updates only when the workflow is saved (Pause, the course's Save steps, Update, autosave), never per step. Otherwise Don't Save would leave the catalog showing a step the saved workflow never reached. - Pause is disabled while a modal dialog is open (for example the gate-name prompt), so a course is never saved halfway through a dialog.

Resume: the saved step id, step history and sub-task progress are restored, plus the panel's tab. Then the step is shown again.

Steps that rely on a window or dialog that isn't saved: resuming checks that the step's spotlight targets are all on screen. If one isn't (it lives in a popup, a dialog, a Compensation sub-page or an unsaved tab), the course resumes on the latest visited step whose targets all show — usually the one that opens them. A step can also name resume_step_id explicitly. The Phase 4 audit found that no course needs one yet: the gate-drawing steps tell the learner to pick the tool themselves, and their _verify steps only check the saved gate.

While locked: the overlay covers the whole panel and takes all input, and the isolated window's menu bar is disabled.

docs.title: FlowSOM — implementation plan
docs.text:
Adds FlowSOM to the Population Analysis tab as a second clustering method next to UMAP + HDBSCAN, and teaches the Sample Lens to audit gates against either one. First, the main tabs are reordered so the last three follow the workflow: Sample Lens → Statistics → Comparisons.

Status record: the phase checklist below. Resume at the first unchecked phase. Commit on main, one commit per phase. Each phase leaves the plugin runnable.

docs.title: What FlowSOM produces
docs.text:
UMAP + HDBSCAN gives every event a 2-D map position and a cluster label, with some events labelled noise (-1). FlowSOM gives something different:

  1. A grid of nodes. A self-organizing map (SOM), by default 10 × 10 = 100 nodes. Each node is a small group of very similar cells, described by its median marker values (its code). Every event is assigned to exactly one node. No event is noise.
  2. A tree of the nodes. A minimum spanning tree (MST) links each node to the nodes most like it. FlowSOM's standard picture is this tree: one circle per node, sized by event count and coloured by a marker or by metacluster. Branches of the tree usually follow lineages.
  3. Metaclusters. The 100 node codes are clustered hierarchically into k metaclusters, which are the populations. Each event's label is its node's metacluster. Because the hierarchy is kept, k can be changed after the run without retraining (re-cutting 100 nodes is instant).

What it does not produce: a 2-D position for each event. To show events on a map, use one of these: - the tree layout, with each event drawn near its node (jittered), as FlowSOM's own plots do; or - an optional UMAP of the same events, computed only for display.

How it compares with HDBSCAN, as a second opinion: - HDBSCAN finds clusters by density and can drop rare or diffuse cells as noise. FlowSOM assigns every cell, so a small population tends to get its own node. - FlowSOM splits the data into as many metaclusters as k asks for. A k that is too high splits one real population in two; a k that is too low merges two. HDBSCAN chooses the number of clusters itself. - FlowSOM is fast: a million events takes seconds, and it needs no UMAP first. It can therefore run on the whole population instead of a subsample.

docs.title: Parameters (Population Analysis, FlowSOM selected)
docs.text:
Parameter Default Meaning Sample, Population, Channels, Run name as UMAP shared with UMAP Events 100% (cap 1,000,000) FlowSOM is fast enough for the whole population Grid size 10 × 10 number of nodes; more nodes gives finer detail Metaclusters (k) 10 expected number of populations; can be changed after the run Training passes 10 passes over the data while the SOM learns Random seed 42 makes a run reproducible

Every parameter but the seed gets a help button in plain language, like the UMAP ones.

docs.title: Reuse (do not rebuild)
docs.text:
Need Reuse Gate filter, subsample, logicle transform the preprocessing in UmapAnalysis.run, pulled out into one shared function Background run, cancel, progress AnalysisBase + task_scheduler, the UmapService pattern Heavy compute off the GUI process daemon_worker (new run_flowsom handler beside run_umap) Storing and saving runs experiment_edits.add_umap_run, store._umap_runs, attachment_manager Cluster stats and marker heatmap the stats block at the end of UmapAnalysis.run Exporting clusters as populations ClusterResultsPanel._create_populations (labels plus indices, method-agnostic already) MST, hierarchical metaclustering scipy.sparse.csgraph.minimum_spanning_tree, scipy.cluster.hierarchy (scipy is already a dependency) Lens audit, gate synthesis, across samples analysis/sample_lens/ unchanged; it works on labels

No new dependency. The SOM is written in NumPy (batch SOM, vectorized). The flowsom Python package is not used: it pulls in anndata and other heavy dependencies, and its licence has to be checked against PolyForm Noncommercial (the same problem PyQt6 had).

docs.title: Design notes
docs.text:
• One run format. A run stays a dict in umap_runs. The storage keys keep their names so old workspaces open unchanged. New field method: "umap_hdbscan" (default when missing) or "flowsom". A FlowSOM run adds:
  • nodes (per event)
  • codes (nodes × channels)
  • grid
  • mst_edges
  • layout (2-D node positions)
  • linkage
  • k

clusters holds the per-event metacluster, so every existing consumer of clusters keeps working. embedding is the jittered tree layout, or the display UMAP when that option is on (embedding_kind: "tree" or "umap"). - A method descriptor, not if-chains. A small ClusteringMethod record per method holds: - display name - cluster noun ("cluster" or "metacluster") - map caption - whether it has noise - whether k can be re-cut

The lens and the results panel read wording from it. This lets the next method (PhenoGraph, hierarchical) slot in as a new descriptor. - Re-cutting k. It changes clusters from linkage in the GUI process. The new labels and k are stored on the run. Clusters already exported are not changed; they are populations now. - Merge findings must allow for over-splitting. With FlowSOM, "this gate holds 2 metaclusters" may just mean k is too high. The lens flags a merge only when the two metaclusters stay separate at a coarser cut (they join high in the hierarchy). Otherwise it stays quiet. The finding text names k. - The UMAP animation is UMAP-only. A FlowSOM run shows the progress bar, then the results. - Tab order is one source of truth. A MainTab enum (in tab order) plus a table from tab to center-stack page and chrome (sidebars, ribbon). It replaces: - the literal indices in main_panel._on_tab_changed_locked and its other setCurrentIndex(6)-style calls; - the TabActiveValidator(n) literals in courses 1–6.

The validator takes a MainTab. Academy pause/resume saves the tab name, and an old saved integer is mapped through the old order.

Done phenotype-aware rather than hierarchy-aware (easier to explain): for FlowSOM, a merge is only flagged when the metaclusters' phenotypes clearly differ (+ against −), a cut only when the kept and lost cells share a phenotype, and findings with one phenotype are grouped. docs.title: Open questions (decide when the phase starts)
docs.text:
• Spectral's position. This plan keeps it after Pipeline. Moving it next to Compensation would also follow the workflow, but it shifts more indices.
  • Default event count. Is the whole population (capped) right, or should FlowSOM match UMAP's subsample so the two runs compare on the same events? Matching makes the lens comparison cleaner; the whole population is FlowSOM's strength.
  • Large exports. Exporting metaclusters from a 1M-event run writes very large SubsetGate index lists into the workspace. This may need a compact encoding before it is the default.

docs.title: PhenoGraph — implementation plan
docs.text:
Adds PhenoGraph to the Population Analysis tab as a third clustering method, next to UMAP + HDBSCAN and FlowSOM. The Sample Lens audits against it, and the lens learns to say when several methods agree. The Academy is reorganised so the three methods fit across two courses.

Status record: the phase checklist below. Resume at the first unchecked phase. Commit on main, one commit per phase. Each phase leaves the plugin runnable.

docs.title: What PhenoGraph does
docs.text:
PhenoGraph (Levine et al., Cell 2015) is graph-based clustering:

  1. Neighbours. For every event, find its k nearest events in marker space (default k = 30).
  2. Shared-neighbour graph. Link two events by how many neighbours they share (Jaccard: shared ÷ combined). Two events in the same population share most neighbours; two events either side of a gap share almost none.
  3. Communities. Leiden finds groups of events that link more to each other than to the rest. The resolution sets how fine the groups are: higher gives more, smaller clusters.

Like FlowSOM, nearly every event gets a cluster. Events that end up in a cluster smaller than a minimum size (default 10) are labelled outliers (-1). Unlike FlowSOM you don't choose the number of clusters, and unlike HDBSCAN nothing is dropped for being sparse.

What it does not produce: a 2-D map position per event, or a tree. What it adds instead is the graph, from which we can say how strongly each pair of clusters is connected (the PAGA idea, Wolf et al. 2019).

docs.title: Measured on the tutorial data
docs.text:
Sample C, Leukocytes, 208,961 events, 4 markers, scratch benchmark:

Step Time Neighbours (pynndescent, k = 30) 8 s Jaccard weights (SciPy) 2.4 s Leiden, per resolution 3 s Resolution Clusters 0.5 15 1.0 32 2.0 57

At 1.0 the B cells are split into many clusters along gradients (a known PhenoGraph trait). A 0.5% B220+ CD3+ CD8+ cluster appears, likely B–T doublets, but not confirmed. The tutorial files have only area channels (FSC-A, SSC-A; no FSC-H/W), so no singlet plot can check it: the Academy presents it as an open question.

docs.title: Licences
docs.text:
Package Role Licence Status pynndescent nearest neighbours BSD-2 already installed (via umap-learn) scipy Jaccard weights, sparse graph BSD-3 already a dependency scikit-network 0.33.5 sknetwork.clustering.Leiden BSD-3 new; needs only numpy + scipy; wheels for cp310–313 on macOS, Windows, Linux; works with our numpy 1.26.4 phenograph — MIT, but requires the two below not used leidenalg — GPL-3 not allowed python-igraph — GPL-2 not allowed

The PhenoGraph steps (neighbours → Jaccard → Leiden → small clusters to -1) are ours, a few dozen lines. Only Leiden comes from scikit-network. scripts/check_license_compliance.py must pass with it added.

docs.title: Parameters (Population Analysis, PhenoGraph selected)
docs.text:
Parameter Default Meaning Sample, Population, Channels, Run name shared as the other methods Events 100% (cap 1,000,000) full population; ~15 s at 200k Neighbours (k) 30 how many neighbours each event links to; higher merges small groups into larger ones Resolution 1.0 how fine the clusters are; can be changed after the run Minimum cluster size 10 smaller clusters become outliers Random seed 42 reproducible neighbour search and Leiden

Each gets a plain-language help button, like the other methods.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
A Cluster Graph tab, first for PhenoGraph runs (like FlowSOM Tree):

  • One circle per cluster, sized by events, coloured by cluster or by a marker (scaled to the clusters' range, like the tree).
  • Edges between clusters, thickness = connectivity (edges between the two clusters in the shared-neighbour graph ÷ what their sizes would predict). Weak edges hidden below a threshold (a slider).
  • Layout: classical MDS + SMACOF on connectivity distances, reusing the FlowSOM layout code.
  • Reading guide, three steps:
  • Thick edges join clusters that are one population cut along a gradient.
  • A cluster with no strong edges is a distinct group, often rare and worth a look.
  • Colour by a marker to name the groups.
  • Resolution control: debounced re-cluster in the background (~3 s), with a progress line. Not instant like FlowSOM's k.
  • The legend and phenotype heatmap reused from FlowSOM (generalised to any clusters), with +/lo/− calls.

Gallery, interactive map, statistics and export work as for the other methods. The map's embedding is the cluster-graph layout with events jittered round their cluster (embedding_kind = "graph"), like FlowSOM's tree. A UMAP map for PhenoGraph runs is left for later (see Decisions).

docs.title: Design notes
docs.text:
• Run format. Same dict in umap_results; method = "phenograph". Added keys:
  • resolution
  • n_neighbors
  • min_cluster_size
  • cluster_edges (pairs + connectivity)
  • layout (per cluster)

clusters holds per-event labels, so every consumer keeps working. - The graph is not saved. At 209k × 30 neighbours it is about 25 MB. On load, changing the resolution rebuilds it once (~10 s, background, with a progress line), then keeps it for the session. - Memory at 1M events. The benchmark's one-shot Jaccard (A[rows]) would build ~900M entries. Compute it in chunks of rows (or in numba), and test 1M events under a time and memory budget. - Where it runs. pynndescent is numba, like UMAP, which runs in the daemon process. Phase 2 confirms whether the task worker thread is safe (as FlowSOM's is) or the daemon is needed. - Method descriptor. Add a ClusteringMethod for PhenoGraph. Generalise "re-cut": - descriptor field recut_param: name, label, range, step and whether re-cutting is instant (k) or a background job (resolution); - the lens's k row becomes a generic row driven by it.

Replace the lens's recuttable checks for "may over-split" with a descriptor flag over_splits (FlowSOM, PhenoGraph), so the phenotype-aware merge/cut rules apply to both. - Determinism. pynndescent with a seed can still vary across thread counts. Test that a seeded run gives the same clusters (adjusted Rand index ≈ 1); if not, document it and seed Leiden at least.

docs.title: Phases
docs.text:
• [x] 0. Dependency. Add scikit-network==0.33.5 to pyproject.toml and lock it. Licence check, SBOM and pip-audit pass. A smoke test imports sknetwork.clustering.Leiden and clusters a toy graph.
  • [x] 1. PhenoGraph core (Qt-free). Found while building: scikit-network's Leiden uses the C library's rand() (unseeded by random_state), so the module seeds it under a lock; the Jaccard count is a numba merge (numba now a direct dependency); the graph holds at most 250k events, the rest take the majority cluster of their 5 nearest graph events (1M events: 25 s, 1.9 GB peak, against 4.3 GB uncapped). Layout helpers moved to layout.py, shared with FlowSOM. analysis/clustering/phenograph.py:
  • knn_graph(x, k, seed): pynndescent, then chunked Jaccard, giving a symmetric CSR graph;
  • leiden(graph, resolution, seed, min_size): labels numbered largest first, small clusters to -1;
  • cluster_connectivity(graph, labels): PAGA-style edges;
  • the cluster layout, reusing the MDS + SMACOF from flowsom.py (moved to a shared helper).

Unit tests on the lens fixture's planted populations: - ARI above a threshold; - more clusters at a higher resolution; - seeded reproducibility; - connectivity is high inside a split population and low between distinct ones; - 1M events within budget. - [x] 2. Run plumbing. Runs in the daemon: in a worker thread the neighbour search and Leiden stalled the GUI thread for up to 1.8 s. The daemon loads the Qt-free clustering package by path and caches the last three runs' graphs by run_uid; after a reload the graph is rebuilt from the run's intensities (equal to rounding, so clusters match to ARI > 0.95). The method descriptor gained RecutSetting (k or resolution), over_splits and tag_prefix. PhenographAnalysis and PhenographParams. run_phenograph() in the service (thread or daemon, per the note above). - recluster_run(run, resolution), as recut_run: exported clusters unchanged, names cleared, tables recomputed. - Persistence in attachment_manager; the graph is rebuilt on demand. - Tests: run → save → load round trip; reclustering after load rebuilds the graph. - [x] 3. Population Analysis UI. The FlowSOM tree's frame (guide, colour by, re-cut control, legend, heatmap, hover) became ClusterMapView; the FlowSOM tree and the PhenoGraph Cluster Graph are subclasses. A cluster with no links is marked "stands apart" in the legend and title. The results panel asks the viewer to re-cluster (recluster_requested) and shows the result (apply_recluster); the spin waits with "Re-clustering…" meanwhile. - "PhenoGraph" in the method combo, with its own parameter panel. - Events slider at 100% for PhenoGraph. - The Cluster Graph tab: guide, colour by, resolution control, edge threshold, legend and heatmap (generalised from the FlowSOM widgets, not copied). - History label: "{i}. {name} · PhenoGraph res=1.0". - Tests: run from the tab with a fake service; changing the resolution refreshes the statistics, the history and the export list. - User checks it live here (first runnable slice). - [x] 4. Sample Lens. One re-cut row for both methods (SampleLensKSpin for FlowSOM, SampleLensResolutionSpin for PhenoGraph); a PhenoGraph re-cluster runs in the background with a status line and re-audits when done. The map draws the cluster links behind the events. On the tutorial data (Sample C, resolution 1.0) the lens reports that DP holds the small B220+ CD3+ cluster (22% of DP): material for the Academy (the cluster stands apart in the graph and lands in a T-cell quadrant). - PhenoGraph runs in the run picker. - The resolution row (generic re-cut row). - Findings name clusters with phenotypes and use the over-split rules. - The map draws the cluster graph with finding clusters ringed. - Tests mirror the FlowSOM lens tests. - [x] 5. Agreement across methods. analysis/sample_lens/agreement.py. Cuts and merges match by kind and gate; a missed cluster matches when the other run's missed cluster holds over half of its events (of those both runs used). Each card shows "Also found by …" or "Only this run finds it". Re-auditing 3 runs on 209k events takes ~0.3 s. On the tutorial data (PhenoGraph res 0.5) the T-cells cuts and the DN merge are also found by FlowSOM; the DP merge (the B220+ CD3+ cluster) only by PhenoGraph. When the open sample has more than one clustering run on the same population, each finding says which other runs report the same kind of finding on the same gate ("Also found by: FlowSOM, PhenoGraph"). Findings found by only one method are marked as such. - A finding is the same if it has the same kind and the same population path; clusters are not compared. - Tests: two runs agreeing, and one disagreeing. - [x] 6. Docs. - 08_POPULATION_ANALYSIS.md: a PhenoGraph section (graph, resolution, reading connectivity, when to prefer it). - A three-method comparison table: noise, cluster count, speed, what each view shows. - 16_SAMPLE_LENS.md: PhenoGraph and the agreement line. - [x] 7. Academy. See below. Dry runs on the tutorial data offscreen, then step and word-limit tests. User plays it live.

docs.title: Academy: three methods across two courses
docs.text:
Course 4 already runs ~65 minutes with UMAP + HDBSCAN and FlowSOM. Adding PhenoGraph there would make it ~85. Recommended:

# Course Change 4 Population Analysis: UMAP + HDBSCAN FlowSOM section moved out; back to ~50 min 5 Sample Lens FlowSOM add-on moved out; unchanged otherwise 6 Second Opinions: FlowSOM & PhenoGraph (new) see below; ~45 min 7 Reporting (old Course 6) renumbered only

New Course 6, after the lens so the lens is already known:

  1. Why a second opinion. Every method makes you choose how fine to cut: minimum cluster size, k, resolution.
  2. FlowSOM. The Course 4 FlowSOM section, moved as is: prediction on noise, run, read the tree by CD3 and B220, k high and to 5, phenotypes.
  3. PhenoGraph.
  4. Prediction: will it find more or fewer clusters than FlowSOM's 10?
  5. Run it on the same Leukocytes, then read the cluster graph: thick edges join split B cells; colour by B220.
  6. Find the isolated small cluster and read its phenotype (B220+ CD3+). Ask what it could be; doublets are one possibility, not the answer. Explain the FSC-H/W check these files can't do.
  7. Change the resolution and watch the B-cell clusters merge.
  8. Three opinions in the lens. Switch runs and read "Also found by". Which finding do all three report? Which only one? Then the existing "Which findings to trust" step.
  9. Prediction reveal and graduation; badge e.g. 🩺 "Second Opinion".

Mechanics:

  • Course ids stay. flow_course_6_reporting keeps its id and becomes Course 7 by order and title. The new course gets flow_course_clustering_methods, so saved progress and badges still match.
  • Prerequisites.
  • The new course requires the lens course.
  • Reporting keeps requiring the lens, not the new course, so anyone part-way through reporting isn't locked out.
  • Order in COURSES sets the numbering.
  • Text. Every "Course N" in texts, course docstrings and 10_ACADEMY_TUTORIALS.md is renumbered. The Course 4 / 5 FlowSOM references move with the steps.
  • Paused progress in removed steps. _resume_point returns a block unchanged when its step no longer exists. Fall back to the latest step in its history that still exists, or the course start. Test it with a saved block pointing at a removed FlowSOM step.

docs.title: Decisions (2026-10-18)
docs.text:
• Academy layout: the table above. FlowSOM moves to the new Course 6 with PhenoGraph; Reporting becomes Course 7.
  • The B220+ CD3+ cluster: the Academy may say it could be doublets, but must not present it as fact. Treat it as a question for the learner, not an answer.
  • No UMAP map for PhenoGraph in this plan. The cluster graph is the method's own view, the gallery and lens use the jittered graph layout (as FlowSOM does), and Course 4's UMAP run is already there to compare with. The optional UMAP stays under Later.
  • Neighbours default 30, not 15. UMAP's 15 sets the map's local detail; HDBSCAN then clusters the map, not that graph, so matching the number doesn't make the methods comparable. In PhenoGraph k sets the grain: on the tutorial data, k = 15 gave 46 clusters at resolution 1.0 against 32 at k = 30, splitting populations further, and saved only ~1.5 s. 30 is PhenoGraph's published default; keep it, with help text saying lower means finer.

docs.title: Later (not in this plan)
docs.text:
• An optional UMAP map for PhenoGraph runs, reusing the neighbour graph.

  • t-SNE (openTSNE, BSD) as an alternative map for any method.

  • MILK (Yachie lab, bioRxiv Aug 2026) once peer-reviewed and packaged; check its licence.
  • Consensus clusters across methods (events every method groups together).

docs.title: Sample Lens — implementation plan
docs.text:
Replaces the "Sample Lens (Demo)" tab with the real feature: one sample, every population, checked against an unsupervised clustering of the same events. Our answer to CytoFLEX's single-sample analysis page.

Status record: the phase checklist below. Resume at the first unchecked phase. One branch (feature/sample-lens-demo), one commit per phase.

docs.title: What the user gets
docs.text:
1. Gating path with backgating. Pick a population: every gate on its path is shown as a live plot of its parent population, with the picked population's events highlighted. Gates on these plots are the real gates — dragging one edits it and propagates it like anywhere else.
  2. Gate audit. Using a UMAP + HDBSCAN run of the sample, each cluster is compared with the final populations. Findings, in plain language: missed population (a cluster no final gate holds), gate merges clusters, gate cuts a cluster.
  3. Across samples. For the picked population: its % parent in every sample that has it, flagged when the gate edge sits in a dense part of that sample's data, or when its % parent is an outlier.
  4. Fix a missed population. Propose ordinary rectangle gates on real channels that recover the cluster; add them to the tree through the gate coordinator (so undo, propagation and stats all work).

docs.title: Reuse (do not rebuild)
docs.text: Need Reuse Population tree / selection ui/widgets/gate_hierarchy.GateHierarchy Gating-path plots, gate editing ui/graph/flow_canvas.FlowCanvas (+ coordinator) UMAP scatter ui/widgets/cluster_scatter_draw.draw_cluster_scatter Population masks GateNode DAG evaluation (mask cache) Same population across samples analysis/population_matching.label_path_index Display transforms analysis/transforms.apply_transform / invert_transform, gate x_scale/y_scale Running UMAP, storing runs UmapService + experiment_edits.add_umap_run Adding gates IGateCoordinator.add_gate Widgets, theming SDK components + theme_manager.apply_style

docs.title: Design notes
docs.text:
• Scope of an audit = the UMAP run. A run covers a subsample (indices) of one population (node_id). Only the leaf populations under that node are judged, and only on the run's events. The UI says so.
  • Final population = leaf of the gate DAG, excluding UMAP-exported cluster nodes (is_umap_parent subtrees) — those come from the clustering itself.
  • Edge density, any gate shape: an event is "on the edge" if nudging it by a small step in display space (±x, ±y) flips its membership. Works for every gate type through Gate.contains, no per-shape geometry.
  • Gate synthesis works in display space (the gate's own channel scales), then converts the box back to raw values for a RectangleGate.
  • Analysis lives in analysis/sample_lens/ and stays Qt-free.

docs.title: Phases
docs.text:
• [x] 1. Analysis core — analysis/sample_lens/: run scope (align a UMAP run with a sample's events and populations), audit, edge density + cross-sample check, gate synthesis. Public GateNode.mask(). Unit tests.
  • [x] 2. Backgating overlay on FlowCanvas — set_backgate(mask, color); 2-D scatter overlay and 1-D highlight through the existing data layer.
  • [x] 3. Sample Lens tab — replaces the demo: sample + run pickers ("Run UMAP + clustering" when none), population list, findings, gating-path strip, UMAP gates-vs-clusters, across-samples table. Live refresh on gate events.
  • [x] 4. Fix a missed population — propose gates for a cluster, preview, add through the coordinator.
  • [x] 5. Docs — user docs page, plan checked off. (The demo tab, never committed, was deleted in phase 3.)
  • [x] 6. Academy Course 5 — tutorials/course5.py (56 steps) between Population Analysis and reporting (now Course 6). Found on the tutorial data first: Course 3's T-cells guide cut the CD4 T cells (guide fixed), logic nodes hid their gates from the final populations, and controls skewed Across samples (both fixed). The sidebar's icicle became an indented PopulationList: a wide tree doesn't fit 340 px. Lens validators in tutorials/validators.py; dry run on the tutorial data passes every check in order.

docs.title: Flow Cytometry — Overview
docs.text:
Karcytics' Flow Cytometry module takes you from raw instrument files (.fcs) all the way to publication-style statistics and figures — loading data, correcting for dye spillover, drawing gates around the cell populations you care about, and comparing them across samples — all inside one workspace.

This page is a map of that workspace. If you'd rather learn by doing than by reading, jump straight to the Academy — a set of built-in, hands-on tutorials that teach the whole module using real sample data Karcytics downloads for you.

New here?

The fastest way to get oriented is the in-app Academy. It walks you through loading files, compensation, and gating step by step, checking your actual work as you go — not just "click Next." See Academy & Guided Tutorials. Prefer a written walkthrough first? Start with Getting Started.

docs.title: What this module does
docs.text:
• Reads real instrument data — native support for FCS 2.0, 3.0, and 3.1 files, with automatic channel and marker detection.
  • Displays fluorescence honestly — true Logicle (biexponential) transforms, so compensated data that dips slightly negative still renders correctly instead of being clipped.
  • Corrects for dye spillover — algorithmic compensation matrices computed from your single-stain controls, or extracted directly from a file's embedded calibration data.
  • Lets you draw any shape of gate — Rectangle, Polygon, Ellipse, Quadrant, and Range gates, organized into a hierarchical gating tree.
  • Calculates the numbers you need — 13+ statistical parameters per population (Count, % Parent, % Total, Median/MFI, CV, and more).
  • Shows your data six different ways — Pseudocolor, Dot Plot, Contour, Density, Histogram, and CDF views of the same population.
  • Goes beyond manual gating — UMAP dimensionality reduction with optional HDBSCAN clustering, so you can validate (or challenge) your manual gates with an unsupervised second opinion.

docs.title: How the workspace is laid out
docs.text:
Every screen in the module shares the same skeleton:

  • Tab bar (top) — switches between the nine work areas described below. The 🎓 Cyto Academy and Save Workspace buttons live at the right-hand end of this bar, always visible no matter which tab you're on.
  • Toolbar ribbon (just under the tab bar) — a strip of buttons specific to whichever tab is active: importing files on Workspace, drawing tools on Gating, and so on.
  • Left sidebar — the Groups panel, the Sample List, and the Gating Hierarchy tree, so you always know which samples exist and which populations you've already carved out of them.
  • Center canvas — your plots. On most tabs this is a tabbed set of 2D graphs; on the Pipeline tab it becomes a flowchart of your gating strategy instead.
  • Right sidebar — the Properties Panel, showing live statistics and settings for whatever sample or gate is currently selected.
  • Footer — a thin status bar across the very bottom that quietly reports what just happened ("Samples loaded," "Gate created," "Compensation applied," …).

Four tabs — Workspace, Gating, Compensation, and Pipeline — keep this sidebar-plus-canvas arrangement and swap in their own ribbon. The other five — Spectral, Population Analysis, Sample Lens, Statistics, and Comparisons — take over the full window as self-contained workspaces, hiding the sidebars entirely because they show data differently (tables, spectra, an analysis console, or comparison charts) rather than a per-sample plot.

docs.title: 1. Workspace
docs.text: This is home base and almost always the first tab you'll touch. Import your .fcs files here, organize them into Groups, and tag each one with a Role (Unstained, Single Stain, FMO Control, Full Panel) so the rest of the module knows how to treat it. Everything downstream — compensation, gating, propagation — depends on decisions made on this tab. → Workspace guide

docs.title: 2. Gating
docs.text: The heart of the module. Draw Rectangle, Polygon, Ellipse, Quadrant, or Range gates directly on your plots to isolate the populations you care about, nested as deep as your biology requires. A live Group Preview shows your gate landing on every other sample in the group as you draw it, and an Auto-Propagate toggle controls whether that happens automatically. → Gating guide

docs.title: 3. Compensation
docs.text: Fluorescent dyes leak a little light into their neighbors' detectors, and this tab is where that gets corrected. Karcytics can extract a spillover matrix straight out of a file's own metadata with one click, or compute one algorithmically from your Single Stain controls — then apply it to every sample at once. Compensated samples get marked with a small ✦ tag so you always know at a glance whether you're looking at raw or corrected data. → Compensation guide

docs.title: 4. Spectral
docs.text: An interactive viewer pulling real fluorophore excitation/emission spectra live from FPbase, so you can see exactly why (or whether) two dyes in your panel actually overlap — hover between two curves for a real overlap-integral percentage. Its Learning Compensation sub-tab is a self-paced interactive slideshow that walks through spillover and matrix math using your own panel's real numbers. → Spectral guide

docs.title: 5. Pipeline
docs.text: Your entire gating strategy, redrawn as a flowchart instead of a nested tree — the same view you'd screenshot to explain your analysis to a collaborator. Drag nodes around, reorient the whole layout, and build AND / OR / NOT logic nodes to combine populations — handy for cross-checking a manual gate against, say, an unsupervised cluster from Population Analysis. → Pipeline guide

docs.title: 6. Population Analysis
docs.text: Where you step outside manual gating. Pick a root population and a set of channels, run UMAP to flatten your multi-dimensional marker data into a 2D map you can color by any channel, and optionally layer on HDBSCAN clustering to let the data group itself with zero manual input. Any resulting cluster can be exported straight back into your gating hierarchy as a real, usable population. → Population Analysis guide

docs.title: 7. Sample Lens
docs.text: A check of one sample's gating strategy. Pick a population to see every gate above it with the population backgated; the lens compares your gates with a UMAP + HDBSCAN clustering of the same cells and flags populations you missed, gates that merge two clusters, and gates that cut one; and it shows the population across every sample, flagging fragile gate edges and outliers. A missed population can be turned into ordinary gates in one click. → Sample Lens guide

docs.title: 8. Statistics
docs.text: A dedicated, full-screen statistics explorer. Pick any combination of populations, samples, and metrics, and view the result as a sortable table or switch it to a Grouped Bar or Heatmap chart for an at-a-glance read. → Statistics guide

docs.title: 9. Comparisons
docs.text: Five dedicated chart types for putting populations and samples side by side: Violin, Channel Heatmap, Radar, and Histogram Overlay (with a Ridge alternative for a handful of series) — each one better suited to a different kind of question than a plain statistics table. → Comparisons guide

docs.title: Learn by doing: the Academy
docs.text:
Every capability described above is also taught hands-on, inside the app, by the Academy — three structured courses that walk you through real UI interactions with on-screen spotlighting, live checks against what you've actually done (not just "click Next"), and their own demo data so you don't need a dataset of your own to get started.

→ Academy & Guided Tutorials

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Getting Started — a written, step-by-step walkthrough from loading your first file to saving your first workflow.
  • Academy & Guided Tutorials — the interactive alternative, complete with sample data.
  • Scientific Logic — the mathematics behind the transforms, compensation, and statistics, for readers who want the underlying rationale.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
The fastest way to learn: the Academy

Before reading any further, consider clicking the 🎓 Cyto Academy button in the top-right of the tab bar. It opens Flow Cytometry Fundamentals, a guided, hands-on course that walks you through everything on this page — loading files, compensation, and your first gating hierarchy — using its own demo data, with Karcytics checking your actual work at every step. See Academy & Guided Tutorials for details on what each course covers.

If you'd rather read through the workflow first (or you're working with your own data right away), this guide walks the same path in writing — the same ground Courses 1 and 2 of the Academy cover, minus the spotlighting and automatic checks.

docs.title: What you'll need
docs.text:
Any .fcs file (FCS 2.0, 3.0, or 3.1) will load. To follow every step below — including compensation and boundary-based gating — you'll ideally have:

  • One Unstained control (no dye — establishes autofluorescence baseline).
  • One or more Single Stain controls (one fluorophore each — used to compute spillover).
  • One FMO (Fluorescence Minus One) control per marker you plan to gate on — every dye except that one, so you can see exactly where true background ends.
  • Your actual experimental samples.

You can still follow along with just your experimental files — you'll simply skip the compensation and FMO-boundary steps.

docs.title: Step 1 — Load your FCS files
docs.text:
Make sure you're on the Workspace tab (the leftmost tab), then click ➕ Add Samples in the ribbon.

  1. A file picker opens — select all the .fcs files you want to work with (multi-select is supported).
  2. If any of the files live outside your current project folder, Karcytics asks whether to copy them into the project's own assets folder. Say yes if you want the project to stay portable and self-contained.
  3. A progress dialog tracks the load. Once it finishes, your files appear in the Sample List on the left, and the footer bar confirms how many samples loaded.

Compensation might already be done for you

If a file has a $SPILL keyword embedded in its header (common for data exported from acquisition software), Karcytics extracts and applies that spillover matrix to every sample automatically the moment they're loaded. Look for a small ✦ tag next to a sample's name in the Sample List — that's your sign it's already compensated. If you don't see it, you'll build a matrix by hand in Step 3.

docs.title: Step 2 — Understand Groups
docs.text:
Before assigning roles, glance at the Groups panel above the Sample List. Every sample you just imported sits in one default group, All Samples. A group is simply a named subset of your samples, and it controls something important: gates you draw on one sample only propagate automatically to other samples in the same group.

For most single-experiment work, the default group is all you need — you don't have to create a custom one. Reach for 📁 Create Group only when you're mixing tissue types or experiments that genuinely need different gating strategies, so their gates don't interfere with each other.

docs.title: Step 3 — Tag every sample with a Role
docs.text:
Roles tell Karcytics what each file is, which drives compensation math and boundary detection later. The core roles are:

Role Meaning Unstained No dye — establishes the autofluorescence baseline Single Stain One dye only — used to compute the spillover matrix FMO Control Every dye except one — reveals the true background for that marker Full Panel A real experimental sample, fully stained Isotype Control Validates antibody specificity

To assign roles one at a time: double-click a sample in the Sample List to open it, then use the Role dropdown in the Properties Panel on the right.
